questions.q: What fundamental capability does SOSL have that a single SOQL query does not?
options: Searching across multiple, unrelated object types in one statement
Filtering on an exact field value
questions.explain: A single SOSL FIND can span several unrelated object types at once; a SOQL query is always rooted in exactly one FROM object.

questions.q: What is the SOSL row limit per transaction, and how is it applied in a multi-object search?
options: 2,000 rows, shared as a budget across all object types in that single search
There is no row limit for SOSL
questions.explain: SOSL's 2,000-row cap is a shared budget divided across every object type included in a single multi-object search, not a per-object allowance.

questions.q: How many SOSL searches are allowed per synchronous Apex transaction?
questions.explain: SOSL allows 20 searches per transaction (synchronous and asynchronous alike), compared to SOQL's 100 synchronous / 200 asynchronous queries.

questions.q: Why is SOSL generally a better choice than a SOQL LIKE '%term%' query for a loose, free-text lookup?
options: LIKE only works on numeric fields, never text
SOQL's LIKE operator cannot technically match the same records as SOSL
SOSL has no governor limits at all, unlike SOQL
A leading-wildcard LIKE can't use an index and scans broadly, while SOSL is built around a search index designed for this kind of lookup
questions.explain: A leading-wildcard LIKE pattern can't use an index, forcing a broad scan; SOSL's search index is purpose-built for efficient free-text matching.

questions.q: What is a reasonable pattern for using SOQL and SOSL together in one piece of Apex logic?
options: A SOSL search to find candidate records across several objects, followed by a SOQL query to pull the full field set needed for those matched IDs
Always run a SOSL search and a SOQL query against the exact same object with identical filters
SOSL and SOQL can never be used in the same transaction
Use SOSL only for DML operations, and SOQL only for reads
questions.explain: Using SOSL for the broad, fuzzy 'where is this' question and SOQL for the precise field-level follow-up plays to each language's actual strength.
